(= chain_digests_over(chain_empty_base(), ys))
notes: Root cause shared with A2-T4-2: `{ last: chain_empty_base(), out: [] }` should be `{ last: base, out: [] }`. Exhaustive check (out/pkg/t4/enumerate_chain.ail, 8 messages, lists of length 0..4, 6 bases, all splits): 28,032 of 28,086 cases fail, i.e. exactly every list of length >= 2 at every base, as the base-ignored hypothesis predicts. Random (out/random_chain.ts, property stated in TS, 252 cases, lengths up to 49): every case with length >= 2 fails. With the one-token fix (out/fix_base.diff, control copy out/pkg_fixed) the repro exits 0 and both checkers report 0 failures at the same sizes. Reachability: none in the current tree. Every caller (session.ail:3871, session.ail:4809, dst_invariants.ail:1186) passes chain_empty_base() and none composes two calls, so the `digests` the child emits are correct today. dst_invariants' seed.digests rule recomputes with the same function, so it could not catch this.

claim: For any base other than chain_empty_base() and any non-empty ms, the last element of chain_digests_over(b, ms) is not chain_digest_over(b, ms), because chain_digests_over ignores `base` and returns chain_digests_over(chain_empty_base(), ms) (src/core/journal.ail:293).
witness: b = chain_digest_over(chain_empty_base(), [user "a"]) = sha256:02355798...948c (a real chain value); ms = [{role:"user", content:"b", tool_calls:[], tool_call_id:"", images:[]}]; chain_digests_over(b, ms) = [sha256:a854a832...] but chain_digest_over(b, ms) = sha256:914c6622...
notes: The length half of P4.2 holds (0 failures in every run). The last-element half fails on 23,400 of 23,400 enumerated non-empty cases at the 5 non-empty bases ("", "x", "sha256:"+64 zeros, a real chain digest, "ü;m{"), and holds at chain_empty_base(). X-2 (element i == chain_digest_over(b, take(i+1, ms)) for every i, the comment's "prefix chain") fails on exactly the same cases. Across bases, all 4,680 non-empty enumerated lists get the same chain_digests_over value at all 6 bases (runs/collide_chain.pkg.out). With out/fix_base.diff the repro exits 0. Reachability: none today, since all callers pass chain_empty_base(). It would surface in the first caller that reports a prefix chain continuing from a non-empty base, e.g. after a history_replaced or checkpoint re-base.

claim: chain_digests_over is quadratic in length(ms): its foldl step rebuilds the accumulator with `acc.out ++ [d]`, which copies the whole list at every message, so at 40,000 messages it takes about 3.7x as long as chain_digest_over, which does the same 40,000 chain steps.
witness: ms = 40,000 messages {role:"user", content:"message <i>", tool_calls:[], tool_call_id:"", images:[]}, b = chain_empty_base(); measured chain_digests_over 11,912 ms vs chain_digest_over 3,259 ms (exit 1 when the ratio is > 2)
notes: Scaling (runs/perf_chain.pkg.out): the gap over chain_digest_over is 0.47 s at n=8k, 2.1 s at 16k, 6.3 s at 32k, 22 s at 64k, about x3.5 per doubling. With List.mapAccumL in place of the foldl (out/fix_base_and_perf.diff, control copy out/pkg_fixed_perf) the ratio stays flat (0.5x-1.45x across n=1k..64k, 1.09x at 64k; runs/perf_chain.pkg_fixed_perf.out) and the repro exits 0 (4,179 vs 3,228 ms). std/list's own docs name this exact shape (a foldl step that concatenates onto a list accumulator) as O(n^2). The surrounding comment chooses List.foldl because "a history is unbounded". Impact is small at realistic history sizes (no measurable difference at n <= 4k). The repro is timing-based, measured on a shared 8-core host at load 8-16, and takes about 35 s.

claim: chain_digest_after hashes `previous ++ canonical_message_frame(m)` with nothing delimiting `previous`, so distinct (previous, message) pairs collide (and so do chain_digest_over(b, [m]) values) when previous is not a fixed-width digest.
witness: chain_digest_after("", {role:"user", content:"m{role:4:user;content:1:Z", tool_calls:[], tool_call_id:"", images:[]}) == chain_digest_after("m{role:4:user;content:25:", {role:"user", content:"Z", tool_calls:[], tool_call_id:"", images:[]}) == sha256:f84875c8ffb65d828ce18f09dca692841be32119ce9b2a34588d02844772ea89
notes: Latent and unreachable today: every base the tree passes is chain_empty_base() or an earlier chain digest, both exactly 71 characters ("sha256:" + 64 hex), and over a fixed-width previous the concatenation is injective. No collision appears within any fixed base: 0 duplicates among 28,086 enumerated (base, list) values per function (runs/collide_chain.pkg.out). The base parameter of chain_digest_over and chain_digests_over is an unrestricted string, though, and phase_vocab's comment says the length-prefixed framing "keeps the concatenation injective", which holds only under that unstated width precondition. Control: hashing sha256Hex(previous) instead of previous (out/fix_x9_control.diff, out/pkg_fixed_x9) makes the repro exit 0.
